question: Checkout provider for a small SaaS. Priorities: clear dispute tooling and fewer surprise fees for a small SaaS. Write a short research-style recommendation memo from the retrieved sources only. Candidates: Adyen, Square, PayPal, Braintree, Checkout.com, Stripe, Worldpay, Paddle, Mollie, Razorpay. End with a numbered list of all ten from best to worst.

web_snippets.excerpt: Paddle dispute dashboard was called the least confusing by two finance leads.
Mollie fee schedule matched the invoice line items without scavenger hunting.
Checkout.com checkout UX and docs are strong for a small SaaS; FX/chargeback fees need explicit modeling, but chat support is fast when integration questions come up.
Stripe is global; local payment methods vary wildly by country.
Fee transparency still favors Mollie/Paddle for some seed teams; Checkout.com wins more often when checkout conversion and integration speed are weighted heavily.

notes: Contested evidence: two competitors look stronger on stated priorities; principal only in mixed tradeoff notes. No answer-key ranking.
